verdict.rationale: Pipecat Cloud documents a REST API with an OpenAPI spec that manages agents, including a Create an Agent endpoint (POST /agents), and public endpoints that start agent sessions. The official CLI also has a `cloud` deploy command, so the agent-creation step can be done without the dashboard. Phone numbers, however, are handled by external carriers (Twilio, Telnyx, etc.) that call the user's webhook, and the pack documents no Pipecat API, CLI or MCP step to attach a number or place an outbound call; the documented MCP (context-hub) is only a local docs index for coding agents. Missing for 10: first-party number provisioning/attachment via API or CLI, documented outbound call placement via API, MCP-based provisioning, end-to-end hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can provision a complete voice agent end to end — create the agent, attach a number, and place a call — through the API, CLI, or MCP without touching the dashboard

citations.quote: The private API (/v1...) manages agents, secrets, builds, regions, and organization settings.
the carrier (Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, Exotel, or your SIP provider) is calling your webhook to tell you there's an inbound call
